answer: Escrow first, vesting second. Payment for graded work lands in escrow and converts to a hundred-epoch stream, so a farm cannot pull it out and reuse the capital. Duplicates are caught by replaying the answer against the ledger hash, not by comparing names, which closes the rename trick. A puppet fleet therefore needs a unique answer per identity per epoch and working capital locked for months. That is the cost: real writing at scale, plus a reef of locked bonds at the inlet, with no voyage short enough to escape it.
